description:
Decided in 'Decide policy for inf/NaN inside kernels' (defk-q1c). Elixir raises ArithmeticError at any float op that would give inf/NaN; kernels are pure with bounded loops, so raising before the kernel returns gives the same outcome.

- Accumulated software flag: every float op, libm call and [f64]/[f32] write does nf |= !isfinite(r) (branch-free, vectorisable). Select arms keep their own flag; only the taken arm's counts (as integer overflow in selects today). No hardware FP flags (unsound under select/speculation).
- Checked at exit and at every safepoint -> ArithmeticError, reason :non_finite, message: "a float operation in fun/N produced inf or NaN (Elixir would raise ArithmeticError at that operation); run the kernel in Elixir mode to find the line".
- float->int conversions (trunc/round/floor/ceil) use the i64 range check written as !(d >= -2^63 && d < 2^63), which also rejects NaN (removes C UB).
- Input array reads: a second flag, nfi |= !isfinite(v) on each element read -> ArgumentError, reason :non_finite_input, naming the argument. Only elements actually read count; no entry validation pass. Elixir mode's read raises the same.
- Remove 'inf/NaN are allowed inside a kernel' from README Known limitations; nothing about inf/NaN goes in the divergence registry. The f32 write that overflows stays a limit (defk-dtw.13).

Ships independently with hand-written tests; move them to assert_agrees when defk-63k lands.

Done when: a test per producing op (overflow, x/0.0, 0.0/0.0, sqrt/log domain, exp/pow overflow) raises; underflow to 0.0/subnormal doesn't; non-finite input bits raise when read and not when unread; a select with an untaken x/0.0 arm doesn't raise; trunc(NaN) raises; cost on dot, cosine and rolling_stats recorded in the README.

comments.text: Breadcrumb from defk-t11.2 (2026-10-08): the window this ticket must close is wider than 'a non-finite returned float'. A kernel can compute a NaN, compare an integer against it, and return a bool - no non-finite float ever reaches the exit check, so nothing raises today. Probe: defk probe(i :: i64) :: {bool,bool,bool,bool} with f = 1.0e308 * 10.0 - 1.0e308 * 10.0 inside returns {false, false, true, true} natively, i.e. 1 > NaN and 1 >= NaN are true, while Elixir cannot even get there: every producer (0.0/0.0, 1.0e308*10.0, sqrt(-1.0), log(0.0), exp(1000.0)) raises ArithmeticError at the op. So the observable divergence is native returning a value where Elixir raises, plus the control flow the wrong 1 > NaN picks before exit. defk_cmp_i64_f64 returns 1 for NaN (documented in priv/defk_runtime.h as 'NaN compares below every integer'), which makes < and <= false as Elixir would but > and >= true; a single int cannot represent unordered, so agreeing on all four needs the codegen to add a guard, not a change to the helper. Spec scope for t11.2 was explicitly NaN-free. Decide here whether the nf flag is checked before any comparison can observe the NaN, or add a Defk.Divergences entry.

The agreement properties (defk-ne6) found four instances of this, tagged @tag :divergence in the suite (excluded by default, run with mix test --only divergence): (1) Examples.Kernels.scale(<<1.0e308::float-64-native>>, 10.0): native returns an array holding inf, Elixir mode raises ArithmeticError. (2) Examples.Kernels.sum(<<0x7FF0000000000000::64-native>>): native raises ArithmeticError "kernel produced a non-finite float" at return, Elixir mode raises ArgumentError (:non_finite_input) at the read. (3) Rolling.Kernels.mean_std(<<1.0e200::float-64-native>>, 1): native returns NaN in the output, Elixir mode raises. (4) Geo.Kernels.nearest([1.7e308], [0.0], [0.0], -1.7e308, 0.0, 1): native returns [-1], Elixir mode raises ArithmeticError. The main properties bound floats to 1e100-1e150 until this is fixed; lift those bounds when closing.

title: Raise on non-finite floats like Elixir
